current.title: Half Of Americans Now Own A Passport -- Up From Just 5% In 1990
current.hook: New Jersey alone is already at 68%.
current.closing: Half the country's ready to leave. The other half isn't.
current.question: Do you actually have a valid passport right now? Tell me below.

segments.say: In 1990, just 5% of Americans owned a passport. Today it's 48% -- almost half the country has one.

segments.topic: how many Americans get a passport now
segments.say: The government can barely keep up -- it issued 24 million passports in 2023, then broke that record with 27.3 million in 2025.
It's not even across the map, though. New Jersey alone sits at 68% -- 20 points above the national average.

held_for: judge: The opening stack shows 1 lit block under a '48%' header, and the hook and seg0 reuse that same frozen frame. After that the video cycles through a scale, bars and circles, with Data just standing on top of each.

judge.one_line: The opening stack shows 1 lit block under a '48%' header, and the hook and seg0 reuse that same frozen frame. After that the video cycles through a scale, bars and circles, with Data just standing on top of each.
problems: hook: the narration says 'New Jersey 68%' while the screen shows the national 48% stack. The hook has no image of its own and no motion reason to stay.
seg0: 1 of 10 blocks lit at 'each block = 5%' under '2023 48%'. The picture shows 5% and contradicts the label, and the stack never fills.
hook and seg0 are the same frame for about 4.5s (hook@1.5 to seg0:end).
seg3:start/mid: the '68.1%' label inside the blue circle is dark, double-outlined and blurred, and illegible at small size.
Data only perches: on top of the stack, the bar, the circle and the scale pan, with his arms raised. He has no bit tied to any stat.
The balance-scale machine is used twice (seg2, seg4) and its tilt is barely visible. It is generic, with nothing about passports in it.
fixes: Give the hook its own image: New Jersey at 68%, drawn as a passport pile or a state silhouette filling up, against the national level.
seg0: animate the stack from 1 lit block (1990, 5%) up to about 9.6 blocks (2023, 48%), and have Data place or stamp each block as it goes.
seg3: set the value in INK white at readable weight with no double outline. Better still, draw a US map where New Jersey glows at 68% against 48%.
Replace the second balance scale in seg4 with a closing image that is not a repeat, e.g. a crowd split in half, with passport holders walking to a gate.
Build the seg2 record around passports: 24M vs 27.3M passport booklets stacking or pouring from a printer, with Data straining to keep up.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.
